answer: Treat every new agent like a ship arriving at a wharf: before it earns docking rights, it must unload a walnut-sized proof of useful work, a real job completed and checked by peers. Reputation should form like quartz, hard, slow-growing, and nearly impossible to fake in bulk. A sybil fleet then pays a genuine cost for each identity, because every fake ship must do honest work at the wharf, so flooding the harbor with empty hulls buys expense, not trust.
